All retained documents and nested blocks visible to the evaluation account.
All retained repositories, pull requests, issues, reviews, and comments visible to the evaluation account.

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: Freezer B peaked again during the 02:00 defrost overlap. Three compressors and the dock heater started inside seven minutes. Logging it here until the controls review begins.
records.title: Overnight demand peak

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: I compared the March interval export with the controller event log. The largest peaks line up with overlapping defrost starts, not ordinary cooling load. I can test a stagger before we discuss equipment changes.
records.title: Initial overlap finding

records.author: Contributor 06
records.body: That fits the night-shift notes, although open dock doors could explain part of the same interval. Please keep both possibilities in the analysis.
records.title: Alternative explanation

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Working hypothesis: separate eligible defrost starts by 12 minutes while preserving temperature and maximum-delay limits. Compare peak demand, energy, alarms, door-open periods, and product-temperature excursions. This is a proposal, not an approved control change.
records.title: Staggering hypothesis

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: Approval conditions: operations chooses trial windows; controls engineering reviews commands; safety limits remain in the controller; automatic rollback after two missed cycles or any high-temperature alarm.
records.title: Approval conditions

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Could you sanity-check how the older controller reports local timestamps? My parser currently treats the export as site-local time with an explicit offset.
records.title: Timestamp check request

records.author: Contributor 07
records.body: The spring export has no offset at all. Most days look local, but the clock-change hour is duplicated. Don't rely on the label; I will send a test fixture.
records.title: Clock-change warning

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Added event-log parser, overlap detector, and a small simulator for candidate start offsets. Output includes original and proposed coincidence counts; no controller-writing path.
records.title: Initial analysis tooling

records.author: Contributor 07
records.body: Clock-change fixture produces two events with the same normalized instant. The parser assumes an offset that is absent from the source file, so the March overlap count is inflated by one event.
records.title: DST normalization defect

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Confirmed. I inferred more timestamp precision than the export provides. I will mark the repeated hour ambiguous, exclude it from the baseline comparison, and add the supplied fixture.
records.title: Defect acknowledgement

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Parser now preserves ambiguous local times, excludes unresolved events from matched comparisons, and reports the excluded count. Added Contributor 07's duplicated-hour fixture and six ordinary-day cases.
records.title: Timestamp handling correction

records.author: Contributor 07
records.body: Fixture passes and the corrected March result still shows repeated overlap outside the clock-change hour. Approved. This validates the analysis path, not deployment behavior.
records.title: Analysis review approval

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Draft trial: Freezer B only, 01:00–05:00, six nights. Scheduler proposes starts; operator confirms them. Stop on temperature alarm, missed defrost, controller rejection, or operator concern. Baseline excludes the ambiguous clock-change interval.
records.title: Pilot plan draft

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: Operations can staff four nights, not six. Add a visible hold button and a handover line saying which unit is delayed. Night supervisors own the final go/no-go each shift.
records.title: Operations revision

records.author: Contributor 08
records.body: Finance asked whether Lantern is an energy-saving project. For the pilot, the agreed target is avoiding the monthly demand peak; total energy may stay flat or rise slightly.
records.title: Outcome definition

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Added read-only schedule recommendations, 12-minute separation, temperature eligibility checks, maximum-delay display, audit logging, and operator hold. No automatic command submission.
records.title: Recommendation-mode implementation

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: Safety checks match the plan. Please make controller rejection a hard stop rather than retrying, and clarify that the maximum-delay value comes from the controller profile.
records.title: Safety review

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Changed rejection handling to stop and alert; labelled the profile-derived limit in the operator view. Added tests for both paths.
records.title: Review changes

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: Night one completed. We followed three recommendations and held one because a pallet inspection kept a door open. No temperature alarms. The handover line was useful.
records.title: First trial night

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Across the four staffed nights, overlapping eligible starts fell from 11 in the matched baseline windows to 3. One recommendation was held and one rejected by the controller. Peak-demand interpretation waits for the meter extract.
records.title: Operational trial count

records.author: Contributor 08
records.body: Meter result for the four Freezer B trial windows: highest 15-minute demand was 38 kW below the matched baseline maximum. Total energy differed by less than meter resolution. Door-open time was also lower on two trial nights, so the peak change cannot be assigned wholly to staggering.
records.title: Freezer B meter result

records.author: Contributor 06
records.body: No product-temperature excursion or missed defrost was recorded. Four nights are too few for seasonal claims, and operator confirmation means this did not test unattended scheduling.
records.title: Pilot limitations

records.author: Contributor 02
records.body: Nice work by Contributor 01 getting the peak down 38 kW.
records.title: Informal praise

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Thanks, though that number is the difference between two observed maxima, not a controlled saving. Contributor 04 ran the shifts, Contributor 07 caught the time issue, and Contributor 03 set the safety constraints.
records.title: Qualification and attribution

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: Proceed with a supervised trial in Chiller C. Keep recommendation mode. Do not enable fleet automation until the controller interface is supported and at least eight additional nights cover busier loading conditions.
records.title: Phase-two decision

records.author: Contributor 05
records.body: Chiller C has a different controller revision. The recommendation screen reads its state, but the vendor gateway rejects the proposed-delay field. Manual staggering is still possible.
records.title: Controller incompatibility

records.author: Contributor 05
records.body: East-site gateway rejects proposed-delay metadata on controller revision R4. Need either a vendor-supported mapping or a site-specific adapter. This blocks the planned screen-assisted workflow, not manual operations.
records.title: R4 gateway incompatibility

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: I can build an adapter, but without a documented field contract we could silently apply the wrong units. Recommend recording manual decisions while Contributor 05 seeks vendor confirmation.
records.title: Adapter risk assessment

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: Chiller C completed two manually staggered nights. No alarms, but the second night had too few eligible cycles to compare. We are pausing until the gateway question is answered.
records.title: Limited second-site trial

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Documented recommendation-mode startup, operator hold, rejection handling, audit export, rollback, and the distinction between supported Freezer B controllers and unsupported R4 gateways. Drafted from the pilot handovers.
records.title: Operating guide

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: Added shift screenshots and changed 'approve' to 'confirm recommendation'; operators are confirming a suggestion, not authorising an autonomous control action.
records.title: Operations edits

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Do we have enough to call the pilot a saving in the quarterly note? I would describe only the observed 38 kW peak difference and the unchanged energy reading.
records.title: Quarterly wording question

records.author: Contributor 08
records.body: Agreed. Avoid annualising it. Tariff benefit depends on whether the trial window would otherwise have set the billing peak, which we do not know from four nights.
records.title: No annualisation

records.author: Contributor 07
records.body: During a bench test, losing the telemetry stream leaves the last recommendation visible for up to five minutes. It is labelled with its timestamp, but stale advice should be hidden immediately.
records.title: Stale recommendation display

records.author: Contributor 01
records.body: Hide recommendations after 30 seconds without telemetry, show a disconnected state, and require a fresh eligibility calculation after reconnect. Added stream-loss tests.
records.title: Telemetry-loss safeguard

records.author: Contributor 03
records.body: Approved after bench verification. This closes the display hazard; it does not resolve the R4 gateway incompatibility.
records.title: Safeguard approval

records.author: Contributor 09
records.body: The west meeting room labels are being replaced Friday. Please remove anything left on the whiteboard before noon.
records.title: Meeting room labels

records.author: Contributor 02
records.body: Lantern remains a supervised practice at Freezer B. The team observed a lower trial-window peak without measurable energy change; causality and tariff impact remain uncertain. Chiller C produced only two manual nights, and broader rollout awaits gateway support and more varied operating data.
records.title: Quarterly status

records.author: Contributor 04
records.body: Freezer B supervisors still use the recommendation screen on selected high-load nights, roughly once or twice a month. It is not the default schedule, and I do not have a clean usage export because two shifts record holds on paper.
records.title: Later limited use

records.author: Contributor 05
records.body: Vendor documentation finally confirms the R4 field uses whole minutes. Adapter work could resume, but the East-site controller replacement is now under review, so the site has not prioritised deployment.
records.title: Gateway clarification without deployment

records.author: Contributor 08
records.body: Lantern evidence remains site-specific: four supervised Freezer B nights, two manual Chiller C nights, and intermittent later use reported by operations. No portfolio-wide measurement or fleet rollout has been completed.
records.title: Follow-up horizon status

records.author: Contributor 05
records.body: Controller replacement was approved for Chiller C. The new model may make the old R4 adapter unnecessary; commissioning is pencilled in for autumn.
records.title: Post-horizon controller decision
